newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures dip but outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures dip but outlook positive.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were down in late dealings but found decent support at lower levels as the market was weighed on by weaker U.S. debt prices.
At 1500 GMT, DTB December Bund futures were down 40 basis points at 99.35 and at the session low in moderate volumes, with strong support pegged at 99.32.

More profit-taking was expected but traders said the market was gearing up for another run toward 100 and for 10-year cash market yields to make an attempt to break down through the six percent level from the current level at about 6.01 percent.
"We are more likely to see 100 again than go below 99," one Frankfurt trader said, noting the correction was expected to end quickly and for the market to soon turn higher.
Market dealings on Tuesday were expected to take their cue from German unemployment data, due at 0855 GMT.
Traders said favourable data could push the market toward resistance at 99.66 and 99.76, while a break below 99.32 could trigger a sell-off toward 99.10 and major resistance at 99.00.
